sections.title: In brief
sections.text: El-Zanfaly and Knight propose a guided learning process that connects fabrication skills with independent design and making.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: Technical machine training alone, they argue, can leave students unable to create beyond simple exercises.

sections.title: How the work approaches it
sections.text: Their I3 process moves from imitation, through constrained iteration, to improvisation. Students first make an existing example, then change one aspect at a time, and finally develop their own work.

sections.title: Evidence and examples
sections.text: The inspected introduction explains the instructional sequence and the instructor’s role. Later cases or evaluation results were unavailable in the readable excerpt.

sections.title: What comes out of it
sections.text: The proposal treats learning to operate tools and learning through material engagement as connected activities. It does not establish measured effectiveness in the inspected passage.

sections.title: Limits to keep in mind
sections.text: No sample size, comparison group or learning outcome can be verified from this excerpt. The related 2015 I3 article must not be substituted for this paper’s missing sections.

sections.title: What to take from it
sections.text: Use the sequence as a reading lens: identify what the learner imitates, what changes between iterations, and when independent decisions become possible.
